title: King Sena IV
biography: Sena IV (954–956 CE) ruled briefly for two years. His tenure sustained administrative and religious infrastructure amid ongoing succession dynamics. The short duration reflects persistent elite volatility in late Anuradhapura.

title: King Kutakanna Tissa
biography: Kutakanna Tissa (44 BCE–22 BCE) restored longer-duration kingship following rapid turnover. His extended reign enabled re-coordination of taxation, temple endowments, and reservoir maintenance cycles. He likely undertook refurbishment of earlier hydraulic structures to stabilize agrarian yield. Reign longevity suggests success in rebuilding elite consensus eroded by preceding instability and integrating monastic interests with palace governance.

title: King Jayavarman VII the Great
biography: Revered as the greatest king of Angkor; established Mahayana Buddhism as the state religion, constructed the fortified city of Angkor Thom with the 216 giant smiling faces of the Bayon temple, and built 102 public hospitals across the realm.
internationalConnections: Constructed a nationwide network of paved highways with resthouses connecting Angkor to Champa and the Gulf of Thailand.

title: King Sena II
biography: Sena II (853–887 CE) enjoyed a robust 34-year reign, one of the longest in late Anuradhapura history. His tenure facilitated sustained infrastructural consolidation: reservoir maintenance, monastic endowments, and administrative routine. His era represents mature 9th-century governance, balancing hydraulic stewardship with Buddhist patronage.

title: Alexander III the Great (Basileus of Macedon)
biography: Undefeated conqueror who overthrew the Persian Empire, founded over twenty cities bearing his name (including Alexandria), and forged an empire from Greece to Egypt and the Indus River by age 32.
internationalConnections: Fused Greek, Persian, Egyptian, and Central Asian cultures, sparking the global Hellenistic Era.

title: Pharaoh Senusret III
biography: One of Egypt's greatest military pharaohs who fortified the southern border in Nubia with massive mudbrick fortresses like Buhen and Semna.
internationalConnections: Dug a navigable canal through the First Cataract of the Nile and conducted campaigns into Canaan.
